title: europe north africa canada wildfires 2026 07 28
text:
LONDON, July 28 (Reuters) - Hello,
Wildfires continue to spread in Europe, North Africa and Canada as firefighters struggle to contain the deadly blazes.
Firefighters were racing to subdue wildfires in France and neighbouring Spain as another heatwave is expected to hit both countries later this week in what has been a blisteringly hot and dry summer across Western Europe.
The CEO of Europe's largest aerial emergency services firm Avincis told ​Reuters that the continent is not ready for longer and more extreme wildfire seasons, as its firefighting aircraft are now needed almost year-round.
ESG Lens looks at what an ‌impending "super" El Niño will mean for countries in Africa, where wildfires have also been spreading in Algeria, Morocco and Tunisia.
Meanwhile, Canada is tackling nearly 900 blazes as of Tuesday, with evacuation orders still in place in First Nation community areas.
‘Fire seasons are getting longer’
Forest fires advanced towards the outskirts of the historic French city of Bordeaux, at the heart of the country's winelands.
About 220,000 people, including tourists and local residents, have been evacuated in France, while in Spain nearly 100,000 were ​told to leave their homes, authorities said.
Temperatures in Bordeaux are forecast to reach 33 degrees Celsius (91 degrees Fahrenheit) during the day, around 7 degrees above the average high between 1961 and 1990, ​according to the Reuters Climate Monitor.
French President Emmanuel Macron has enlisted the military to support exhausted firefighters, amid a record-breaking heatwave that had already resulted in nearly ⁠6,000 excess deaths.
Avincis CEO John Boag said longer European wildfire seasons and bureaucratic obstacles have exacerbated regional shortages of both aircraft and pilots.
"Globally, fire seasons are getting longer, aircraft are not moving between areas and ​pilots are becoming harder and harder to get," Boag said in an interview.
‘No help from Mother Nature’
In North Africa, Algeria’s Civil Protection unit
, opens new tab
 said it has succeeded in extinguishing 34 fires out of 56 recorded across ​several of the country's wilayas, while Tunisia’s Civil Protection and Forestry teams are battling a wildfire that broke out over the weekend in Jebel Dallaj, Henchir Chedly, in Takelsa.
Moroccan authorities also extinguished forest fires in the provinces of Tetouan in the north and Taroudant in the centre of the country after they burned around 12 hectares (30 acres) of forest cover, with no casualties reported, the National Agency for Water and Forests told local press.
Meanwhile, a new report
, opens new tab
 by the University of ​Chicago’s Climate Impact Lab found that about 377,000 people will die each year in countries trapped by extreme heat and lack of access to cooling, with most of these deaths occurring in sub-Saharan Africa ​and Southern Asia where there is less electricity than in wealthier regions.
In North America, roughly 878 fires were burning across Canada on Tuesday, and more than 3.7 million hectares had burned so far in 2026, according to the Canadian ‌Wildland Fire Information ⁠System dashboard
, opens new tab
.
"There is no significant help from Mother Nature whatsoever in the foreseeable future," said Incident Commander Hugh Murdoch of a cluster of fires near Kimberley, B.C., 520 km (323 miles) from Vancouver.
Fires have caused extensive damage in Namaygoosisagagun and Whitewater Lake First Nations in northwestern Ontario and forced evacuations in other communities.
Talking Points
ESG Lens
Forecasters are warning that ​El Niño, which often drives severe droughts, flooding and storms in Africa, could become one of the strongest ever seen if Pacific Ocean warming trends continue.
"Just this event is going to reduce heavily affected countries' GDP by 1% to 2% on average, which is ​about $10 billion to $20 billion across the continent," Anthony Nyong, the AfDB's director for climate change and green growth, said in an interview. Click here for the full Reuters story.
